signals.claim: U.S. transformer supply remained structurally tight entering December 2024, with long lead times sustained by grid replacement, electrification and data-center demand while manufacturers were still adding capacity.

evidence.summary: DOE's November Electricity Advisory Committee meeting included a dedicated Distribution Transformer Shortage Mitigation presentation, showing that transformer supply remained an active reliability/supply-chain issue.

Skanska's Fall 2024 construction-trends report put liquid-filled pad-mounted transformer lead times at roughly 59-130 weeks and said strong data-center/electrification demand was consuming new capacity.

contraryEvidence.summary: New manufacturing capacity was being added across the industry, so extreme lead times should not be assumed permanent.

causalChain: aging grid + electrification + data-center load -> sustained transformer orders
customization/qualification + factory/labor constraints -> long lead times
qualified suppliers with North-American product fit and available/exportable capacity gain orders
local U.S./Mexico capacity can extend capture if it comes online before shortage normalizes
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: A transformer supplier already selling the exact North-American distribution-transformer products in shortage, with multiple customers, growing orders, existing export capacity plus local capacity under construction, and current earnings material enough to justify valuation.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: Potentially expands for qualified transformer manufacturers with deliverable capacity and customer access.
opportunityAssessment.duration: Multi-quarter to multi-year, but normalization depends on new U.S./Mexico capacity and lead-time compression.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: By late 2024 the transformer shortage was no longer obscure; the opportunity requires company-specific earnings acceleration and a valuation bridge.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: Whether incremental North-American orders and local capacity can grow profit faster than industry capacity normalizes.

candidates.name: 伊戈尔
candidates.economicExposure: By November 27 the company explicitly said its U.S. factory was planned for distribution transformers and its Mexico factory for power transformers. Earlier disclosures showed direct North-American transformer sales and multiple customers.
candidates.monetization: 2024Q1-Q3 revenue rose 28.78% YoY and attributable net profit rose 27.21%; operating cash flow rose 53.38%. The earnings bridge is already visible, while U.S./Mexico local capacity remained under construction.
earningsBridge: existing export production plus local capacity ramp

basisReconciliation.externalIndicator: U.S. distribution/pad-mounted transformer lead times and shortage.
basisReconciliation.companyRealizedBasis: Company explicitly identified U.S. plant product as distribution transformers and had direct North-American transformer customers; Q1-Q3 group revenue/profit growth provides realized economic evidence.
basisReconciliation.basisRisk: Not every U.S. utility specification is necessarily addressable, and local factories were not yet fully productive.

candidates.balanceSheetCycle: The thesis depends on order/capacity execution, not inventory-price gains. Overseas capex and ramp timing are key cash-flow risks.
candidates.competitiveQuality: Existing overseas customer base, customized transformer know-how, direct U.S. product fit and local-capacity plans improve the moat relative to generic transformer adjacency.

valuationBridge.marketCapOrEV: Pre-signal market cap about RMB6.54bn at RMB16.65/share.
valuationBridge.bearCase: RMB240m annual net profit (~27.3x P/E), allowing for slower overseas capacity ramp and weaker Q4 conversion.
valuationBridge.baseCase: RMB300m annual net profit (~21.8x P/E), modestly above the simple annualization of Q1-Q3 profit.
valuationBridge.upsideCase: RMB380m annual net profit (~17.2x P/E) if North-American transformer orders and scale utilization continue to grow into 2025.
valuationBridge.impliedExpectation: The cutoff price already requires continued growth, but does not require full U.S./Mexico capacity success. The valuation is not cheap in an absolute cyclical sense; Candidate status depends on the structural multi-quarter order/capacity thesis.

horizonBridge.expectedHalfLife: The bottleneck should persist for multiple quarters and potentially years, but should weaken as new U.S./Mexico manufacturing capacity becomes productive.
normalizationIndicators: U.S. transformer lead times fall materially
U.S./Mexico industry capacity additions reach production
horizonBridge.whyHorizonMatches: The thesis is tied to multi-quarter order conversion and overseas capacity ramp rather than a one-week commodity repricing.

candidates.priceExpectation: The stock was down about 2.4% over 20 days and 6.7% over 60 days, while Q1-Q3 revenue/profit/cash flow had grown. At ~23.3x simple annualized Q3 earnings, the setup is moderately priced rather than distressed; the thesis requires durable North-American transformer growth.
contraryEvidence: Industry capacity additions can compress lead times.
Company local U.S./Mexico capacity was still under construction.
Q3 single-quarter profit declined YoY even though YTD profit grew.
thesisBreakers: North-American transformer lead times normalize faster than expected
U.S./Mexico capacity qualification or ramp is delayed
North-American order growth fails to translate into group profit growth
pre-signal valuation already requires aggressive future earnings
unansweredQuestions: How much of current backlog/revenue is specifically North-American distribution transformers?
What profit level is implied by the cutoff share price?

signals.claim: China's December 3 U.S.-specific ban on dual-use antimony exports tightened an already constrained antimony trade regime, while domestic producers still showed constrained operating conditions and uneven output.

evidence.summary: China's Commerce Ministry notice took immediate effect and in principle prohibited relevant dual-use antimony, gallium, germanium and superhard-material exports to the United States.
SMM estimated November antimony-ingot production rose only 4.59% MoM after two months of declines; 11 of 33 surveyed producers were halted and 19 reduced production.

contraryEvidence.summary: November output did rebound modestly and SMM noted anticipated additional production cuts had not materialized, so the domestic physical squeeze was not uniformly worsening.

causalChain: U.S.-specific export ban -> ex-China availability can tighten further
Chinese producer benefit is not automatic because export channels are restricted
domestic operating miners benefit only if high domestic/product realization plus owned output outweigh lost export optionality
mine output and realized gross profit matter more than headline overseas antimony price
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: An operating Chinese antimony miner with rising proven self-produced output, material antimony gross profit, low dependence on direct U.S. exports, acceptable mine-grade execution and a valuation that does not require permanent extreme antimony prices.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: Scarce operating resources may gain value, but policy can simultaneously restrict producer monetization channels.
opportunityAssessment.duration: Multi-quarter if mine supply remains constrained; policy duration is uncertain.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: The September controls and rising antimony narrative were already known. December adds a U.S.-specific escalation, so only company-level output/valuation improvements justify a new Candidate.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: Whether producer realized earnings rise enough after policy/channel effects.

candidates.name: 湖南黄金
candidates.economicExposure: 2024Q1-Q3 attributable net profit reached RMB666.8m, up 73.56% YoY. H1 antimony segment gross profit was economically material and the company has established antimony mining/refining capacity.
candidates.monetization: Existing output can monetize strong domestic antimony pricing, but self-produced antimony volume had been weak earlier in 2024 and export restrictions are not automatically positive.
earningsBridge: company realized antimony price and self-produced volume

basisReconciliation.externalIndicator: Critical-mineral export controls and constrained domestic antimony production.
basisReconciliation.companyRealizedBasis: Company has material operating antimony production/refining and disclosed antimony segment economics; group Q1-Q3 profit accelerated strongly.
basisReconciliation.basisRisk: Policy restricts exports and the company also has large gold/trading exposure; antimony price does not map one-for-one to group EPS.

candidates.balanceSheetCycle: Operating cash flow lagged profit earlier in the year, so earnings quality and working capital remain relevant.
candidates.competitiveQuality: Established integrated antimony mining/refining is harder to replicate than resource-only optionality.

horizonBridge.expectedHalfLife: Several quarters if global mine supply remains constrained, but substitution, recycling and mine restarts can shorten it.
normalizationIndicators: self-produced company antimony volume fails to recover
horizonBridge.whyHorizonMatches: The edge depends on a policy/supply squeeze feeding through realized quarterly product margins, not a permanent architecture shift.

candidates.priceExpectation: At roughly 25x simple annualized Q1-Q3 earnings after +23.5% 60-day and +50.1% 180-day price appreciation, the stock does not offer enough margin for export-policy and self-produced-volume uncertainty. Remain Watch.
contraryEvidence: Export bans can hurt direct overseas sales
antimony is not the only driver of group earnings
thesisBreakers: valuation already prices a sustained extreme antimony margin
unansweredQuestions: What Q4 self-produced antimony volume was visible by the cutoff?

candidates.name: 华钰矿业
candidates.economicExposure: 2024Q1-Q3 revenue rose 31.62% and attributable net profit 22.62%. By Dec. 5 the company said TALCO Gold production was proceeding to plan after earlier low-grade issues from processing byproduct ore.
candidates.monetization: Large domestic/overseas antimony resources and operating TALCO production create substantial upside sensitivity, but mine-grade/recovery execution remained a first-order risk.
earningsBridge: TALCO and domestic antimony output actually produced and sold

basisReconciliation.companyRealizedBasis: Company operates antimony-bearing mines and said TALCO production was proceeding according to plan; Q1-Q3 earnings growth was already visible.
basisReconciliation.basisRisk: Resource endowment is not equivalent to saleable metal. Ore grade, recovery, throughput and product sales are the gating basis.

candidates.balanceSheetCycle: Small earnings base creates high operating leverage and high execution sensitivity; overseas mine risk is more important than commodity inventory.
candidates.competitiveQuality: Large antimony resource base can be scarce, but only proven operating output deserves full earnings credit.

horizonBridge.expectedHalfLife: Several quarters if antimony scarcity persists and TALCO production ramps; shorter if mine supply normalizes.
horizonBridge.whyHorizonMatches: Quarterly mine output and realized price need time to flow through earnings, but commodity scarcity can normalize within a year.

candidates.priceExpectation: At roughly 60x simple annualized Q1-Q3 earnings after +41.3% 60-day and +81.2% 180-day appreciation, unresolved mine-grade/output risk is not adequately compensated. Remain Watch.
contraryEvidence: Earlier TALCO ore-grade concerns were real
Q3 profit growth was modest despite high antimony prices
thesisBreakers: valuation requires full design output before it is proven
unansweredQuestions: What annualized saleable antimony output could be defended using only cutoff-known data?

finalDecision.noTradeReason: NO TRADE. The policy/supply signal is real, but point-in-time valuation and producer-specific realization/output risks leave neither direct name above Watch.

signals.claim: AI training-server demand was driving strong high-capacity enterprise SSD procurement and price growth, while consumer NAND recovery remained incomplete.

evidence.summary: TrendForce reported enterprise SSD revenue up 28.6% QoQ in 3Q24, procurement capacity up 15%, and strong high-capacity demand from AI training servers.

contraryEvidence.summary: TrendForce expected Q4 enterprise SSD revenue to decline sequentially as procurement peaks passed and server OEM orders were trimmed.

causalChain: AI training servers -> higher-capacity enterprise SSD demand
supplier capacity/shipments lag -> price and revenue growth
profit accrues to qualified enterprise SSD suppliers
A-share opportunity requires direct enterprise SSD shipment economics, not generic NAND exposure
signals.beneficiaryArchetype: An uncontaminated A-share company with material qualified enterprise-SSD shipments, enterprise-specific revenue/profit sensitivity and a valuation bridge independent of broad consumer NAND recovery.

opportunityAssessment.profitPoolChange: Positive for enterprise SSD suppliers but selective.
opportunityAssessment.duration: Structural AI-storage demand overlapped with a near-term procurement peak, so duration is mixed.
opportunityAssessment.expectationGap: Industry growth was visible; direct A-share mapping is the main constraint.
opportunityAssessment.keyUncertainty: Whether any uncontaminated A-share issuer had material enterprise-SSD earnings at the cutoff.

finalDecision.noTradeReason: NO TRADE. Previously evaluated direct storage names are quarantined and no uncontaminated A-share company with material enterprise-SSD-specific earnings proof was established.
